raw_recipe.headline: Jesse's Ginger Salad Dressing
raw_recipe.description: Ready in less than 10 minutes, this dressing is made with a blend of mayonnaise, ginger, soy sauce, and carrot.
raw_recipe.name: Jesse's Ginger Salad Dressing

recipeInstructions.text: Combine carrot, mayonnaise, ground ginger, soy sauce, and sugar in a food processor. Blend until smooth.

review.reviewBody: This is a great basic recipe. I tasted it as written and thought it was really good- especially for such a simple recipe! I did add some things to my final dressing though: 1/8 ts. garlic JUICE, 1t white rice vinegar, 3 drops sesame oil- these additions (at least for me) made this dressing PERFECT!

I was becoming bored with bottled salad dressings and decided to give this recipe a try. I love that it only has a few ingredients and ones that I normally have on hand. (I always keep a bottle of minced ginger in my fridge.) Following the suggestions of other reviewers, I added just a little rice vinegar and sesame oil. I mixed the ingredients in the individual serving jar with my Ninja blender and it came out smooth and creamy. Both my husband and I loved the taste!

I too could drink this stuff. I did use fresh ginger and stevia instead of sugar. I also used 1/2 light and 1/2 full flavor mayo just because I was emptying a jar of light mayo. If you wanted to save calories, you could probably just use light mayo. Wonderful recipe. My kids loved it on baked fish.

Definitely use real ginger & double it.1 TBS of rice vinegar as others mentioned is spot on. I did try the sesame oil as others suggested. However, in my opinion, it does NOT belong in this dressing. Even just a splash totally ruined the flavor. (Let's save that for the dark ginger dressings. Otherwise, it tastes just like the ginger dressing at our local hibachi. Don't blend very long. I pureed mine first time around. Next time, I pulsed just until carrots and gingery were finely chopped, as it should be.
This was the perfect base! I used honey instead of sugar and added extra ginger, wasabi paste and some white wine vinegar (didn't have rice wine). Soooo good! (:

Absolutely amazing! Been trying to find the perfect ginger dressing like our favorite sushi restaurant. I used fresh ginger, added some sesame oil, used two sweet n low instead of sugar and some half n half to make it smoother. Our new fav!!

I loved it. Made it with 2 TBS fresh ginger. Put everything including ginger in Vitamix. Nice ginger taste ., just like Japanese sushi restaurants. We had a salad in Hawaii - Japanese influence - made from water cress , grated carrots and firm tofu that I made and served with this dressing ..It was a hit. Too bad it's mostly mayo. I might try it with Greek yogurt instead.
Loved this recipe! I used fresh ginger, honey, rice vinegar, and about 1 T. of lime juice. It was so good! Oh, and I used a blender because I don't have a food processor and it turned out fine.
This is good as is, but I added more ginger (fresh grated instead of the ground) and a little extra sugar and a splash of rice wine vinegar. This made it so much better. Thanks for the recipe!

I'm not a fan of changing recipes then reviewing them, especially since I gave it five stars but this is a very good recipe, just needed a little extra. Used fresh ginger instead of powdered and added rice vinegar (a good tablespoon or so) and a dash of sesame oil. WOW!! What a great dressing!! Used it on fresh spinach and it was perfect!! The flavors are identical to the restaurant type but since its mayo based, stays creamy. This will definitely be one of my "go to" dressings!!

I used fresh ginger. We didn't have a food processor so we used our blender. It turned out great! THe recipe tastes just like our fgavorite Japaneese steakhouse ginger dressing. This is AWESOME!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Absolutely amazing! Been trying to find the perfect ginger dressing like our favorite sushi restaurant. I used fresh ginger, added some sesame oil, used two sweet n low instead of sugar and some half n half to make it smoother. Our new fav!!
I enjoyed the recipe!!! It was just what I needed to add to my rotisserie chicken!!! Made the most flavorful chicken salad!!!
Are the recipe quantities correct? Mine turned out really dark and thick. Pretty tasty though.

Delicious. I did make the changes suggested by others to bring it up to 5 starts for me. I doubled the recipe and added sessame oil and vinegar. My husband was using a teaspoon to to taste test it several times!!

Easy and tasty. I used fresh ginger and low sodium soy sauce (it’s all I had). Didn’t measure and you can tweak to your taste. The last ginger dressing recipe I tried was a lot of work and ingredients and not anywhere near as good as this one.
This is a fantastic recipe! 4 stars because I had to add a dash of garlic powder and 1 1/2T rice wine vinegar. Otherwise, it is on point!
I’ve been looking all over for this recipe sooooo good thank you
Super simple and delicious. This is closer to the "hibachi restaurant" dressing flavor than any other recipe I've tried.
I made two previous recipes from AR and this was the closest to what we get at the hibachi restraunt. I did no changes or substitutions just followed the recipe. Thank you for the recipe, it's great!
